abstract_html: In the membrane proposal of Nekrasov and Okounkov, the variable that counts the Euler characteristic of a stable pair on a threefold is a rotation fugacity of an ambient Calabi–Yau fivefold. We prove the predicted exchange of these roles for two circle actions over a smooth curve of positive genus. One fixes a local Calabi–Yau threefold with two normal lines of equal degree. The other fixes the product of the curve with a plane. With the orientations determined by the ordered normal lines, their stable-pair indices agree in every positive curve degree as integral classes on the common space of cycles, throughout the Picard variety of splittings. On the product threefold a deformation of the matrix equations makes the virtual contribution vanish above the minimum Euler characteristic. At the minimum, the rotation weights of plane Hilbert schemes reproduce the known local-curve partition function. For a doubled genus-two curve the connected index is supported where the two transverse points coincide. A first variation of the rotation weights detects the same nonzero multiple of the Picard theta class in both descriptions, although the corresponding coefficient vanishes on every individual target.
